rationale: The core definition (a set is finite when equinumerous with a natural number; |A| is the unique such natural) is the standard one. Convention deltas: the source uses {1,...,n} while this item uses the von Neumann natural n = {0,...,n-1}, and the item merges four derived consequences (|n|=n, |A|=0 iff A empty, transport along a bijection, |A|=|B| iff A approx B) into the definition. Merged and renotated, hence ai-altered rather than exact. Proof component = the inline uniqueness argument and the four consequence proofs, locally written from lem-pigeonhole claim 3.

Every clause is sourced separately: Sylvestre Fact 3 gives 'every subset A of B is finite, with |A| <= |B|'; the Finite_set article gives 'any injective function between two finite sets of the same cardinality is also surjective' and the surjection converse, and 'any proper subset of a finite set S is finite and has fewer elements'. The item merges these into one four-clause theorem and restates the proper-subset clause as the equality form |B|=|A| iff B=A (equivalent). Merge plus reformulation, so ai-altered. Proof is the local induction on the ambient natural number.

The recursive definition of a finite sum and product with empty sum 0 and empty product 1 is standard. Deltas: the construction is carried out inside N via the recursion theorem with the index carried in a pair (a local device forced by the one-variable recursion theorem in this library), and the truncated difference n-m is fixed here as a page-wide convention. Semantically the standard object, so ai-altered. Proof component = the inline uniqueness/first-coordinate induction, locally written.

Clauses 1-5 are the standard finite-sum laws (additivity, constant, splitting, monotonicity, product laws) and clauses 0, 6, 7 are the standard facts that the canonical map N -> F is additive, multiplicative, strictly increasing and injective on an ordered field. No single source states this eight-clause list; it is a merge of standard material, renotated with iota and with the zero cases separated out because lem-of-naturals-positive is stated for m,n >= 1 only. Proof is local induction throughout.

The Summation article states the reindexing law 'for a bijection sigma from a finite set A onto a set B: sum_{n in B} f(n) = sum_{m in A} f(sigma(m))', which is exactly permutation invariance. This item specialises it to a bijection pi : n -> n of an initial segment and states it simultaneously for the four operations (R,+), (R,.), (N,+), (N,.). Specialisation plus merge, so ai-altered. The proof device (the increasing deletion map d^n_j and claim (A)) is locally engineered.

Defining sum_{i in S} a_i by choosing an enumeration and appealing to permutation invariance for well-definedness is the standard construction and is exactly what the Summation article's bijection-reindexing clause licenses. Deltas: the item is stated for both R-valued and N-valued summands and adds three named clauses (bridge to the initial-segment sum, reindexing, empty index set / constant summand). Merged and renotated, so ai-altered. Proof component = the inline independence-of-enumeration verification, locally written.

Clauses 1 and 2 are the rule of sum verbatim in content: 'for disjoint sets A and B, |A union B| = |A| + |B|' and, for pairwise disjoint S_1..S_n, '|S_1| + ... + |S_n| = |S_1 union ... union S_n|'. Clause 3 (splitting a sum over a finite index set along a partition of that index set) is the standard grouping law for finite sums. The three are merged into one theorem, and clause 2 is stated over an arbitrary finite index set rather than a natural-number range. Merge plus generalisation, so ai-altered. Proof (the splice map used twice) is local.

Clause 1 is the rule of product verbatim in content: '|S_1| . |S_2| ... |S_n| = |S_1 x S_2 x ... x S_n|' specialised to two factors. Clause 2 is a genuine reformulation: instead of an iterated Cartesian product it uses the set of choice functions with domain m, which is not the source's formulation although it is the standard set-theoretic replacement for it. Reformulated and merged, so ai-altered. Proof (slicing over B, then a restriction/extension bijection) is local.

The recursion m^0 = 1, m^{sigma(n)} = m^n . m and the laws m^{p+q} = m^p m^q, (mp)^q = m^q p^q are the standard definition and laws of natural-number exponentiation, with 0^0 = 1 as the standard empty-product convention. Deltas: clauses (d) and (e) are library bridges (iota(m^n) = iota(m)^n and m^n = prod_{k<n} m) with no direct source. Merged and renotated, so ai-altered. All the inline inductions are local.

The Twelvefold way article gives the count of all functions from an n-set to an x-set as x^n, with no restriction, which is exactly |A^B| = |A|^{|B|} for finite A and B. The two sentences about the degenerate cases (B empty, and A empty with B nonempty) elaborate the same statement rather than changing it, so the edit is cosmetic. Proof is the local induction on |B| with the restriction/extension bijection.

'If S is a finite set with |S| = n, then |P(S)| = 2^n' is exact (Power_set article; Sylvestre Theorem 1). The item merges with it the second clause n < 2^n, deduced from Cantor's theorem, which the same article states for every set. Merge, so ai-altered. Proof is ai-altered rather than ai-generated because the characteristic-function bijection P(S) -> {0,1}^S it uses is exactly the argument the Power_set article gives; the deduction of n < 2^n from Cantor plus pigeonhole is local.

0! = 1 with F(sigma(n)) = F(n).sigma(n) is the standard factorial recursion, and the Falling_and_rising_factorials article gives (x)_0 = 1, the product form x(x-1)...(x-n+1), n! = (n)_n and (n)_k = 0 for k > n. Delta: the source recursion is (x)_n = x.(x-1)_{n-1}, peeling the top factor, while this item recurses on the bottom factor as n^{sigma(k)} = n^{k}.(n-k) with a truncated difference, which is an equivalent but different recursion and is what makes the k > n regime automatic. Renotated and merged with four derived clauses, so ai-altered.

The Falling_and_rising_factorials article states that (x)_n 'gives the number of n-permutations from an x-element set, or equivalently the number of injective functions from a set of size n to a set of size x', with the convention that (n)_k = 0 when k > n; the Twelvefold way article gives the same count as x^{n underline}. This is the item's statement, including both boundary readings (k = 0 and k > n). Cosmetic edits only. Proof is the local induction on |B|.

'An n-element set has n! permutations' is the standard sourced statement and is clause 1 here. The item merges with it the two-set form: |Bij(X,Y)| = n! when |X| = |Y| = n, and Bij(X,Y) empty otherwise. That form is routine but is not the sourced statement, so merged, hence ai-altered. Proof is local (Bij(A) = Inj(A,A) by clause 4 of thm-subset-of-a-finite-set, then the falling-factorial count at k = n).

The Binomial_coefficient article's combinatorial definition is that C(n,k) 'equals the count of k-element subsets within an n-element set', which is exactly binom(n,k) := |[n]^k| here. The [A]^k notation for the set of k-element subsets is standard. The boundary values C(n,0) = C(n,n) = 1, C(n,k) = 0 for k > n and C(n,1) = n are the source's own boundary conventions, read off the definition rather than stipulated. Cosmetic edits only. No proof component: the well-definedness paragraphs are part of the construction.

All four assertions are sourced: C(n,k) = n!/(k!(n-k)!) for 0 <= k <= n, C(n,k).k! = n(n-1)...(n-k+1), integrality, and C(n,k) = C(n,n-k) for 0 <= k <= n. Delta: the primary form here is the division-free identity C(n,k).k!.(n-k)! = n! in N, because binom is a count and R-division is only reached through iota. Cleared of division, merged into four clauses and renotated, so ai-altered. Proof is ai-altered: the double count of Bij(n) by the image of the initial segment is the standard double-counting argument for this identity.

Clause 1 is Pascal's rule under a pure index shift: the source states C(n-1,k) + C(n-1,k-1) = C(n,k) for positive n,k with 'no restriction on the relative sizes of n and k', which under n -> n+1, k -> k+1 is exactly this item's C(n+1,k+1) = C(n,k) + C(n,k+1) for all n,k in N. Clause 2 is the hockey-stick identity, sourced as sum_{i=r}^{n} C(i,r) = C(n+1,r+1) for n >= r >= 0; the item drops the hypothesis n >= k and starts the index at i = 0, a strict generalisation (the extra terms vanish). Merge plus generalisation, so ai-altered.

C(n,2) = n(n-1)/2 is standard. Deltas: the primary statement here is the division-free 2.C(n,2) = n(n-1) in N, asserted for every n in N including 0 and 1 via the truncated difference, with the real quotient form recorded as a consequence through iota. Renotated and extended to the degenerate n, so ai-altered. Proof is a local case split at n = 0, 1 and n >= 2.

The classical binomial theorem (x+y)^n = sum_{k=0}^{n} C(n,k) x^k y^{n-k} for all reals x,y and n in N. Sole delta: the coefficient is written iota(C(n,k)) because a binomial coefficient here is a von Neumann natural and not an element of R, and the statement is confined to R because rings are later in the reading order. Renotated, so ai-altered. Proof is ai-altered: induction from Pascal's rule is the standard proof, but the index bookkeeping (the shifted list b, the range extension using C(n,sigma(n)) = 0) is locally engineered.

Both clauses are sourced exactly, including the hypothesis: the Binomial_coefficient article gives sum_{k=0}^{n} C(n,k) = 2^n and gives the alternating row sum as 0 'for all n > 0', matching this item's n >= 1. Deltas: clause 1 is stated in N and clause 2 in R with iota, and the two are merged with an explicit note that clause 2 fails at n = 0. Merged and renotated, so ai-altered. Proof is ai-altered: the counting proof (partition the power set by subset size) and the substitution x = -1, y = 1 into the binomial theorem are both the standard arguments.

The source states 'C(m+n,r) = sum_{k=0}^{r} C(m,k) C(n,r-k)' for any nonnegative integers r, m, n. This item states C(m+n,k) = sum_{i<k+1} C(m,i) C(n,k-i) for all m,n,k in N with no range restriction: the same identity, the same hypotheses and the same index range, differing only in the names of the bound variables and in writing the upper limit as i < k+1. Cosmetic edits only. Proof is the local double count over M = m x {0}, N = n x {1} partitioned by |S intersect M|.

The source gives the multinomial coefficient's combinatorial meaning as 'the number of ways of depositing n distinct objects into m distinct bins, with k_1 objects in the first bin, ...', which is exactly |B(A,k)| here. Delta: the source defines the coefficient by the quotient n!/(k_1!...k_m!) and derives the count, whereas this item takes the count as the definition and proves the quotient formula in thm-multinomial-theorem; the fibre-of-a-colouring presentation and the named set W(n,m) are local. Definitional inversion plus reformulation, so ai-altered.

Clause 2 is the classical multinomial theorem with the outer sum indexed by nonnegative integer tuples summing to n, renotated with iota on the coefficient. Clause 1 is the source's *definition* n!/(k_1!...k_m!) turned into a theorem, and cleared of division as binom(n,k).prod k_i! = n!, because this library defines the coefficient as a count. Merge, definitional inversion and renotation, so ai-altered. The proof (a colouring bijection for clause 1, and induction on the number of parts through the binomial theorem for clause 2) is locally constructed.

The source defines a composition of n into k parts as an ordered sequence of k positive integers summing to n, and a weak composition as the same with nonnegative parts, and states explicitly that the parts are ordered. This item's definitions of C(n,m) and W(n,m) match term for term, and the item adopts the source's own naming convention (weak = zeros allowed). The finiteness paragraph and the m = 0 and m = 1 boundary values are computed elaborations, not changes to the definition. No proof component.

Both formulas are exact in the source: C(n+k-1,k-1) weak compositions and C(n-1,k-1) compositions. Convention deltas: the source states both 'for any pair of positive integers n and k', while this item asserts the weak count for every n in N (including n = 0, where it gives C(m-1,m-1) = 1, correct) under m >= 1 only, and keeps m >= 1 and n >= 1 for the strict count exactly as the source has it. The item also merges in an explicit bijection onto the M-element subsets of n+M. Generalisation plus merge, so ai-altered. Proof is a local hockey-stick induction with surjectivity of the bijection read off the count.

Novel construction, and deliberately so: this is a page-local editorial ledger of conventions and deferrals, composed for this page; no established result corresponds to it, so it is genuinely AI-composed rather than merely unsourced. An editorial ledger of the page's own conventions and of what is deferred; it states no mathematical proposition that a source could carry. Every assertion was checked against the item it names and holds: N contains 0 and the three hypothesis-bearing results are correctly named; |A| is defined for finite A only; empty sum 0, empty product 1, 0! = 1 and 0^0 = 1 are each the base clause of a recursion carried out on this page (def-nat-finite-sum-and-product, def-factorial-and-falling-factorial clause (a), def-nat-power clause (a)) and each agrees with def-finite-sum and def-integer-power; the truncated-difference convention matches def-nat-finite-sum-and-product; the integrality claim matches thm-binomial-closed-formula clause 2. The closing claim that no item on the page depends on anything named in the deferral section was checked against the deps of all 26 A-page items and holds. No source URL is claimed.

The displayed array is rows 0 to 6 of Pascal's triangle exactly as the source tabulates them. Delta: the particular package of checks around it (four interior entries re-derived from the closed formula, the row sums, and the alternating row sums including the exceptional row 0) is locally chosen. All arithmetic re-verified: rows sum to 1,2,4,8,16,32,64; alternating sums are 1,0,0,0,0,0,0; C(4,2).2!.2! = 24 = 4!, C(5,2).2!.3! = 120 = 5!, C(6,2).2!.4! = 720 = 6!, C(6,3).3!.3! = 720 = 6!.

Novel construction: the worked instance (a 10-element set, selections of size 3) is chosen for this page. The identities it exercises are established, but no source presents this instance, and the item asserts no result beyond the instance. A locally chosen worked instance (a 10-element set, selections of size 3). Directly verified from its stated dependencies: 10! = 3628800, 3!.7! = 6.5040 = 30240, and 30240.120 = 3628800, so C(10,3) = 120 by thm-binomial-closed-formula clause 1; and 10^{1 underline} = 10, 10^{2 underline} = 90, 10^{3 underline} = 720 by the falling-factorial recursion, with 120.6 = 720 confirming C(10,3).3! = 10^{3 underline}. No source is claimed for the particular instance; the Combination URL supports only the underlying identity.

The MISSISSIPPI count is the classical worked instance of the source's statement that the multinomial coefficient 'counts distinct permutations of a multiset with n total elements, where the ith element appears k_i times'. Arithmetic re-verified: 1+4+4+2 = 11, 11! = 39916800, 1!.4!.4!.2! = 1.24.24.2 = 1152, and 1152.34650 = 39916800, so binom(11;1,4,4,2) = 34650. The modelling step (an arrangement is literally an element of B(A,k)) is a local reformulation in this library's colouring language, so ai-altered rather than exact.

Both figures are the sourced ones: the total number of distinct five-card hands from a 52-card deck is C(52,5) = 2598960, and the source's own frequency table gives 5148 flushes (4 royal + 36 other straight flushes + 5108 remaining flushes), which is the count of hands with all five cards of one suit. Arithmetic re-verified: 52.51.50.49.48 = 311875200 = 120.2598960; 13.12.11.10.9 = 154440 = 120.1287; 4.1287 = 5148. Delta: the deck is modelled as 13 x 4 and the item deliberately claims no probability, so the framing is local; ai-altered.

Novel construction: the worked instance (n = 4, m = 3, with the full enumeration and four exhibited images of the stars-and-bars map) is chosen for this page; the theorem it exercises is established but this instance is not a sourced example. A locally chosen instance (n = 4, m = 3). Directly verified: the listed 15 triples are exactly the weak compositions of 4 into 3 parts, organised by k_0 = 4,3,2,1,0 with block sizes 1,2,3,4,5 summing to 15; C(6,2).2!.4! = 15.2.24 = 720 = 6!, so C(6,2) = 15; exactly three triples have all parts nonzero, matching C(3,2) = 3; and the four exhibited images under S(k) = {k_0, k_0+k_1+1} are correct, giving {4,5}, {2,4}, {1,4} and {0,1}. No source is claimed for the particular instance.

Novel construction: the worked instance (the explicit list of all eight functions 3 -> 2, and the eight subsets of a 3-element set) is chosen for this page; the counts it exercises are established but this enumeration is not a sourced example. A locally chosen instance (all functions 3 -> 2, the injections 3 -> 2, and the subsets of a 3-element set). Directly verified: the eight listed triples are exhaustive and distinct; none is injective, matching 2^{3 underline} = 2^{2 underline}.(2-2) = 2.0 = 0 and pigeonhole claim 2 at 2 < 3; the eight subsets group as 1,3,3,1 = 8 = 2^3, matching row 3 of Pascal's triangle and clause 1 of cor-binomial-theorem-consequences. No source is claimed for the particular instance.

Novel construction: the worked instance (m = 4, n = 3, at k = 3 and again at k = 5 to exercise the vanishing terms) is chosen for this page; Vandermonde is established but this pair of checks is not a sourced example. A locally chosen instance (m = 4, n = 3, at k = 3 and k = 5). Directly verified: C(7,3).3!.4! = 35.6.24 = 5040 = 7!, so C(7,3) = 35, and 1 + 12 + 18 + 4 = 35; C(7,5).5!.2! = 21.240 = 5040, so C(7,5) = 21, and the six terms at k = 5 are 0, 0, 6, 12, 3, 0 summing to 21, with the vanishing ones exactly those where 5-i > 3 or i > 4. No source is claimed for the particular instance.

Novel construction: the witness pair A = 2 = {0,1} and B = [2]^1 = {{0},{1}} is bespoke to this page. The surrounding observation that equinumerosity does not single out a bijection is established, so this is a borderline call recorded for Alpha; the classification follows the witness, which is invented. A locally chosen witness (A = 2 = {0,1} and B = [2]^1 = {{0},{1}}) for the standard observation that equinumerosity does not distinguish a bijection. Directly verified from its stated dependencies: |A| = 2 by |n| = n; |B| = C(2,1) = 2; the two exhibited maps are bijections and are distinct; and thm-number-of-bijections-of-a-finite-set gives exactly 2! = 2 bijections, so those two are all of them. No source is claimed for the particular witness.

Novel construction: the witness (the subsets of {0,1,2,3} containing 0 and those containing 1, inside P(X)) is bespoke to this page; the underlying inclusion-exclusion phenomenon is established but this witness is not a sourced example. A locally chosen witness inside P({0,1,2,3}) for the failure of the sum rule without disjointness. Directly verified: |A_0| = |A_1| = 2^3 = 8 by the exhibited bijections onto P({1,2,3}) and P({0,2,3}); |P(X)| = 2^4 = 16; C = P({2,3}) has 4 elements; hence |A_0 union A_1| = 16 - 4 = 12 not 16. One incidental claim in step 3.1 is false and is reported in the findings file. No source is claimed for the particular witness.

The refuted claim is precisely the assertion that no set is Dedekind-infinite, and the witness (the successor map on N, injective and missing 0) is the canonical textbook witness given in the Dedekind-infinite_set article; the Finite_set article supplies the true finite version that the item locates as the missing hypothesis. Delta: the diagnosis of exactly where finiteness is spent in the proof of thm-subset-of-a-finite-set clause 4 is local. Renotated and merged with that diagnosis, so ai-altered.

Not novel: the construction is the rule of sum with its disjointness hypothesis deleted, and both halves are located in the literature. The Rule_of_sum article states the law only 'provided that the intersection of the sets is without any elements', and Sylvestre Fact 4 gives the correction |A union B| = |A| + |B| - |A intersect B|, which is exactly the excess this item measures. Recoverable restatement of established material, hence ai-altered; the two minimal witnesses are a local choice, not a new claim. Verified: |{0} union {0}| = 1 but 1+1 = 2; |{0,1} union {1,2}| = 3 but 2+2 = 4; the excess is 1 = |intersection| in both.

Not novel: the substantial witness is the canonical one. The Countable_set article states that 'the Cartesian product of two sets of natural numbers, N x N, is countably infinite', i.e. N x N approx N, which is precisely the refutation of A prec A x B; the Rule_of_product article supplies the finite law being over-generalised, and the Cardinality article supplies the contrast with Cantor's theorem drawn in the Remarks. Recoverable restatement of established material, hence ai-altered. Verified from stated dependencies: A = B = N gives A approx A x B; A = empty, B = 2 gives empty x B = empty; and the corrected finite statement holds because ab >= 2a = a+a >= a+1 > a for a >= 1, b >= 2.

Not novel: the construction is the sourced identity with its own sourced hypothesis deleted. The Binomial_coefficient article states the alternating row sum sum_{k=0}^{n} (-1)^k C(n,k) = 0 'for all n > 0', so the excluded index n = 0 is located in the literature, not invented here. Recoverable alteration of an established result, hence ai-altered. Verified: at n = 0 the sum runs over k < 1 and is the single term (-1)^0 . iota(C(0,0)) = 1 != 0, and the derivation fails at exactly one evaluation, (-1+1)^0 = 0^0 = 1 rather than 0.

Not novel: the construction is the sourced formula with its own sourced hypothesis deleted. The Stars_and_bars article states the weak-composition count C(n+k-1,k-1) 'for any pair of positive integers n and k', so k = 0 (here m = 0) is located in the literature as excluded, not invented here. Recoverable alteration of an established result, hence ai-altered. Verified at (n,m) = (1,0): the only function 0 -> N is the empty function, whose sum is the empty sum 0 != 1, so |W(1,0)| = 0, while under this page's truncated difference n+m-1 = 0 and m-1 = 0, giving C(0,0) = 1; under the integer reading m-1 = -1 is not a natural and the symbol is undefined.
